title: ALMA Observations of the DART Impact: Characterizing the Ejecta at Submillimeter Wavelengths
question: Measure Didymos-Dimorphos' millimeter spectral emissivity pre-impact, then isolate the DART impact ejecta post-impact to derive dust mass and gas-phase upper limits

data.arrays: ALMA 12 m array pre-impact; simultaneous 12 m array and ACA post-impact

recipe.method: Standard CASA calibration; automated phase (and where possible amplitude) self-calibration; flux scale of J0238+1636 corrected for 12 m Execution 3
key_parameters: gaincal combine='scan,spw' fallback used for all observations

recipe.method: MTMFS continuum imaging with Briggs weighting; Högbom natural-weighted line cubes; auto-masking; primary beam correction; channel-averaged continuum MS to 250 MHz channels for post-impact

recipe.goal: Fit the pre-impact point-source flux density
recipe.method: uvmodelfit point-source model fit to visibilities, compared with image flux

recipe.goal: Derive millimeter spectral emissivity with NEATM
recipe.method: NEATM with subsolar temperature and surface temperature distribution; integrated flux equation solved for emissivity using fit flux and Daly2023 diameters
key_parameters: Bond albedo 0.067; beaming parameter 1.93; Tss = 324 K pre-impact
assumptions: Didymos and Dimorphos have the same spectral emissivity; no emission from the night side

recipe.goal: Predict asteroid flux on the impact date
recipe.method: Repeat NEATM at impact-date geometry; reduce flux for secondary eclipse
key_parameters: rH = 1.045 au, Delta = 0.075 au, Tss = 330 K; eclipse reduction 0.049 mag gives 2.60 mJy
assumptions: Emissivity from pre-impact measurement applies post-impact

recipe.goal: Measure post-impact continuum flux in apertures
recipe.method: Integrate flux inside 50 km radius (12 m) and 200 km radius (ACA) apertures; examine visibility amplitudes versus baseline
key_parameters: Apertures capture all emission at >=3 sigma

recipe.goal: Subtract asteroid flux to isolate ejecta flux
recipe.method: Subtract predicted asteroid flux (2.74 mJy, or 2.60 mJy in eclipse) from each execution's flux

recipe.goal: Compute grain absorption efficiency and dust opacity
recipe.method: Mie theory for spherical homogeneous grains with miepython; porous grains via two-component Maxwell-Garnett (hollow sphere); opacity integrated over size distribution
key_parameters: amin 0.5 um, amax 2.5 cm; a^-2.7 to 2 mm, a^-3.7 above; rho 3500 kg m^-3; porosity 8.2%
assumptions: Grain temperature independent of size and equal to blackbody equilibrium temperature of 266 K at 1.045 au; size distribution and chemistry uniform in the field of view

recipe.goal: Convert ejecta flux to dust mass
recipe.method: Rayleigh-Jeans relation S = 2kTM kappa/(lambda^2 Delta^2) solved for M for each execution and material; weighted average over executions
key_parameters: Three compositions: crystalline olivine (Cry-Oli), amorphous olivine (Amo-Oli), amorphous pyroxene (Amo-Pyr)
assumptions: Weighted average treated as a lower limit on ejecta dust mass; crystalline favored

recipe.goal: Derive spectral-line upper limits and gas-phase masses
recipe.method: 3 sigma integrated intensity limits in a 4.68'' diameter aperture; convert to upper-level and total column densities and vapor masses with Trot = 1000 K
assumptions: Gas rotational temperature 1000 K; gas extended perpendicular to line of sight filtered out so limits constrain line-of-sight emission
